title: SH-201 EP — estimated opening excerpt
method: Source-only analysis: mono 22050 Hz decoding of the original Roland MP3, 8192-sample Hann STFT at 256-sample hops, nonnegative least-squares decomposition against detune-broadened harmonic templates over MIDI 36–88, and inspection of local FFT peaks and amplitude transitions. Candidate notes were screened for upper-harmonic and subharmonic errors. Local FFTs distinguish played-note fundamentals from the unusually loud third harmonics: D4 produces ~294/882 Hz, G4 ~392/1176 Hz, D5 ~587/1761 Hz, and G5 ~784/2352 Hz. The opening rising figure D4–G4–D5–G5–G4–D5 sits above a G3 accompaniment. The next groups use Bb3 with F4–G4–C5, Eb3 with Bb3–G4–D5–G5–G4–D5, and F3 with C4–G4–D5. Onsets are roughly quarter-second steps from 0.082 seconds, with two-second accompaniment changes.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable. Every event here is estimated from the MP3, not an exact original MIDI event.
Velocity 100 is an explicit placeholder. Original velocities, sustain pedal, pitch bend, modulation and other controller events are unavailable and are not recovered.

Sounding pitch families do not uniquely determine played keys when oscillator octave offsets or layered tones are unknown. This transcription uses sounding fundamentals with a newly designed patch at zero overall transpose.
MP3 encoding, detuned oscillators, effects and envelope release obscure key-down and key-up times. The MIDI contains practical gates, not measured hardware key releases.
The patch is newly authored in Septum from spectral and temporal cues. It is an approximation of the named factory sound, not Roland factory SysEx or a recovered hardware preset.
Bass accompaniment and melody share overlapping harmonics; ringing previous notes can mask exact releases. The estimated melody uses 235 ms gates with long patch decay.
Odd partials are part of the timbre, not extra high MIDI notes. The original patch’s oscillator interval, ring modulation or feedback setting remains unknown.
Sustain-pedal use is unknown. The excerpt ends in the fourth group’s release tail.

patch_design.name: APX 201 EP
rationale: A sine at the played pitch multiplied by an octave-up sine generates fundamental and third-harmonic components; a small direct octave component supplies the observed even partial. This is an explicit synthesis hypothesis for the EP’s bell-like spectrum.
A fast attack and long decay approximate the struck-key envelope; light modulated delay adds the small frequency spread seen around upper partials.
uncertainties: No authenticated factory PRESET dump is available; every changed control value is an authored approximation.
The recording does not uniquely reveal oscillator topology, layer routing, filter slope, modulation or effect settings.
The ring-modulation topology is a deliberately chosen way to reproduce observed partial families, not a recovered fact about Roland’s preset.
Third-harmonic level and frequency-dependent decay will differ from the unknown factory design.
